findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/AssertEvents.java:~482 — `isAccessTokenId` matcher has inverted logic and a wrong offset: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` returns *false on a match* and checks chars 3–4 instead of the grant shortcut at chars 4–5 (`substring(4, 6)`). Net effect: the matcher only verifies "something:UUID" format and never actually validates the expected grant shortcut, so all the updated assertions (code/device/CIBA/refresh) give false confidence; it would also throw `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of returning false for a prefix shorter than 5 chars.

[Low/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/AccessTokenContext.java:~76 — copy-paste error in the constructor: the fourth check is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` — it validates `grantType` twice and never validates `rawTokenId`, so a null rawTokenId silently passes and later produces token IDs like `onrtac:null`.

[Low/doc_defect] server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:~30 — the `getShortcut()` javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", but `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider` hard-codes 2-char segments and a 6-char prefix (`encodedContext.length() != 6` check). A provider following the javadoc produces token IDs that `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects with `IllegalArgumentException`; there is also no shortcut-length validation at registration time.

[Low/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:~118–135 — the lazy "refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed" paths in `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` insert into `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` without the duplicate-shortcut validation performed in `postInit`. A runtime-deployed grant whose shortcut collides with an existing one silently overwrites the mapping, so previously issued token IDs decode to the wrong grant type.

[Low/api] server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:~33 — `getShortcut()` was added as a new abstract method to the provider factory interface. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` calls `getShortcut()` on every registered `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, so any existing third-party grant provider compiled against the old interface will throw `AbstractMethodError` and fail server startup. A `default` method would have preserved compatibility (server-spi-private, hence Low).

[Low/bug] server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantType.java:~102–107 — `Context.grantType` is captured from form params only in the constructor, but the class retains `setFormParams(...)`, which replaces `formParams` without recomputing `grantType`. If form params are ever swapped after construction, the context carries a stale grant type that gets written into the client-session attribute in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`.

[Low/test_gap] services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java — the unit test only covers encode/decode round-trips; `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (the actual session-type/offline/lightweight/grant-type classification logic, including the `UNKNOWN` fallback) and the factory's `postInit` duplicate-shortcut detection have no test coverage.

goldens.comment: In AccessTokenContext constructor, the fourth Objects.requireNonNull validates grantType twice instead of validating rawTokenId, allowing null rawTokenId values to pass validation.

In isAccessTokenId, the substring for the grant shortcut and the equality check look inverted: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4–5 (substring(4,6)), and a match should return true (combined with UUID check), not false.

Javadoc mentions "usually like 3-letters shortcut" but some implementations use 2-letter shortcuts ("ac", "cc", "rt", "te", "pc", "ci", "ro"). Consider updating documentation to reflect actual usage pattern.
Catching generic RuntimeException is too broad. The implementation throws IllegalArgumentException specifically - catch that instead for more precise testing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:~118–135 — the lazy "refresh maps in case new grant type was deployed" paths in `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` insert into `grantsByShortcuts`/`grantsToShortcuts` without the duplicate-shortcut validation performed in `postInit`. adjudication.rationale: In DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.getShortcutByGrantType() and getGrantTypeByShortcut(), the “refresh maps” logic uses ConcurrentHashMap.put(...) to add/update grantsByShortcuts/grantsToShortcuts without any duplicate-shortcut detection like the size-check performed in postInit(). If a newly discovered/runtime-added OAuth2GrantTypeFactory returns a shortcut already used by another grant, grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType) will overwrite the existing mapping for that shortcut, so later decoding in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.getTokenContextFromTokenId() can resolve the same 2-char shortcut to a different grant type than when tokens were issued.

A `default` method would have preserved compatibility (server-spi-private, hence Low).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `String getShortcut()` to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` (server-spi-private). In `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit`, the code iterates all registered `OAuth2GrantType` factories, casts to `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory`, and unconditionally calls `gtf.getShortcut()`. Any existing provider factory implementation compiled against the previous interface (without `getShortcut()`) would not have that method and would throw `AbstractMethodError` when invoked, potentially failing startup during `postInit`. No `default` implementation is provided to preserve binary compatibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantType.java:~102–107 — `Context.grantType` is captured from form params only in the constructor, but the class retains `setFormParams(...)`, which replaces `formParams` without recomputing `grantType`. If form params are ever swapped after construction, the context carries a stale grant type that gets written into the client-session attribute in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse`.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `OAuth2GrantType.Context` now caches `grantType` once in the constructor (`this.grantType = formParams.getFirst(OAuth2Constants.GRANT_TYPE);`) and exposes `getGrantType()`. The class still has `setFormParams(...)`, but nothing in the diff shows `grantType` being recomputed when `formParams` is replaced. Since `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse(...)` writes `context.getGrantType()` into `clientSessionCtx` (`clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, context.getGrantType());`), a later `setFormParams(...)` call could make the cached `grantType` inconsistent with the current `formParams`. The diff does not show whether `setFormParams(...)` is actually used after construction, so the defect impact can't be verified here, but the inconsistency is real and review-relevant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] services/src/test/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest.java — the unit test only covers encode/decode round-trips; `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` (the actual session-type/offline/lightweight/grant-type classification logic, including the `UNKNOWN` fallback) and the factory's `postInit` duplicate-shortcut detection have no test coverage.

adjudication.rationale: Verified from the diff: `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderTest` only exercises `getTokenContextFromTokenId()` and `encodeTokenId()` round-trips (e.g., `testSuccessClientCredentialsToken`, `testOldToken`). It does not call `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider#getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext(...)`, which contains nontrivial classification logic for session type (TRANSIENT/OFFLINE/ONLINE), token type (LIGHTWEIGHT/REGULAR via `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)`), and the `UNKNOWN` fallback when `clientSessionContext.getAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, String.class)` is null. Also, the new `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory#postInit(...)` logic that builds shortcut maps from `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory#getShortcut()` and throws on duplicate shortcuts (`if (grantsByShortcuts.size() != grantsToShortcuts.size()) throw ...`) has no test coverage shown in this diff. This is a concrete test gap for newly added behavior, not a functional defect by itself.
